summary: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who earned degrees at the universities of Würzburg and Münster. She held professorships at Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University (appointed 1988).

Eliz Hale works in religious and Buddhist studies. Hale earned a B.S. at the University of Mississippi (2018–2022), a Ph.D. at UC Davis (2023), and is attested as a graduate student at UC Santa Barbara in 2026.

Eliza Marian Butler studied at Newnham College, Cambridge (~1909–1913). She held posts at the University of Manchester (1936), Owens College (~1936–1945), and the University of Cambridge (~1945–1951).

Elizabeth A. Cecil, an Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology scholar, earned degrees at Hastings College, UT Knoxville, and Brown University under James L. Fitzgerald. She taught at Leiden, Groningen, and became Assistant Professor at Florida State University in 2018.

Elizabeth Colton Spooner was an Indology scholar who studied at Harvard University under Charles Rockwell Lanman, as well as at Yale University, Radcliffe College, and the American Institute of Sacred Literature.

Elizabeth De Michelis is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from SOAS and the University of Cambridge. She served as director at Cambridge (2000) and was appointed to the theology faculty at the University of Oxford.

Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Oxford in 1999 under the supervision of Alexis Sanderson, having also studied under Harunaga Isaacson.

Elizabeth Errington works in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Johannesburg School of Art and SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar, and served as curator of pre-Islamic coins at the British Museum from 1993.

Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Canterbury in 1994 and served as a tutor in religious studies at the University of Otago, attested in 2007.

Elizabeth J. Harris is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She completed her doctorate under Ananda Guruge and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, later holding posts at Westminster College and the University of Birmingham.

Elizabeth J. Perry is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1978). She held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1978–1990) and Harvard University (~1997).

Elizabeth Morrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her Ph.D. at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. She taught at Amherst College (1998–1999) before joining Middlebury College in 2003.

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner and served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project, attested from 2001 to 2006.
Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality. She served as director at the University of Winchester in 2021.

Elke Rogersdotter is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at Umeå University, attested in 2006, supervised by Thomas B. Larsson and Bozena Werbart, with co-advisors Karin Viklund and P. Ajithprasad.

Ellen M. Raven is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She held posts at Leiden University, attested in 2003 and 2018, and served on the editorial board of Gonda Indological Studies, attested in 2018.

Elliot M. Stern is an Indology scholar who earned doctorates at the University of Pennsylvania (1988, 1998) under George Cardona and Wilhelm Halbfass, having also studied under traditional teacher P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri (1978–1979).

Elliot Sperling was a Tibetology, sinology, and history scholar who earned his degrees at Queens College and Indiana University Bloomington. He served as associate professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1987–2015) and held posts at Harvard and Delhi.

Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Fred Pfeil. She held posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford, attested in 1989.

Ellwood Austin Welden was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Harvard, Berlin, Bologna, and Penn (Ph.D. 1906). He held posts at Bryn Mawr College (1910), Lawrenceville School (~1916–1919), the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce (1923–1927), and Maine.
